summary: Across 597.5 minutes, 12 experiments completed, including 4 compute-bound experiments. The listed tail peaks at 196.27 minutes for synthesis work and at 102.48 minutes for compute work; the locked task-level field reports no compute-bound GPU-idle condition.

The compute tail includes 102.48-minute admission-gated and 50.93-minute fixture-gated entries; the data supplies no phase breakdown, so their durations cannot be causally assigned to gate waiting, setup, or model execution.
The absence of per-task time-series GPU and model-concurrency evidence prevents utilization measurement and runner-selection attribution.
improvements_suggested: Add gate-aware phase timing to every experiment receipt, separating readiness wait, environment or model setup, execution, verification, and artifact persistence.
Record task-correlated GPU utilization, active model count, and runner identity throughout compute-bound experiments.
Make transition evidence and collision-free identity allocation incremental and resumable, then compare the next measured duration with the 196.27-minute entry.
Dispatch through DualGPURunner only when a task declares at least 2 models intended to run in parallel; retain single-GPU execution for single-model work.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Build an incremental, resumable transition and identity-allocation path for the longest listed task.
Emit phase-level gate, setup, execution, verification, and artifact-write timers in experiment receipts.
Attach continuous GPU samples, active-model count, and runner identity to compute-bound receipts, with conditional DualGPURunner dispatch for parallel-model tasks.
meta_reflection: The bounded evidence ranks the visible runtime tail and rules out a task-level GPU-idle flag, but it does not reveal why the compute entries ran long or whether parallel-model execution occurred. A nonzero savings estimate would be unsupported until phase and concurrency telemetry is recorded.
